Cloudflare CEO Sees "an Even Higher Gear" After Q3 Revenue Jumps 39% ©@jittawit21 from jittawit21 via Canva; @3alexd from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cloudflare's third-quarter revenue rose 39% to $782.5 million, its fastest growth in nearly four years and $46 million above its own guidance midpoint.

Management guided fourth-quarter revenue to $845 million to $846 million and expects a GAAP profit in that quarter, well ahead of its 2028 target.

Growth is getting more expensive: cost of revenue jumped 54%, and GAAP gross margin fell to 71.2% from 74.0%.

The fourth-quarter report, expected in February, will show whether the GAAP profit lands and gross margin stops sliding.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) just posted its best quarter ever, and it landed in an ugly week for AI stocks. Cloudflare said on November 5 that third-quarter revenue rose 39% to $782.5 million.

That result gives investors a fresh comparison with Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ), a close software peer that reported a day earlier. In the second quarter, both companies grew revenue 36%, although Datadog did it on $1.12 billion of sales.

Cloudflare shares rallied after the report anyway. The wider AI trade had sold off on fears of tougher data center rules after Democrats swept the midterms. On Monday, Morgan Stanley and UBS called that rout overdone, and Wall Street bounced.

The harder question sits under the beat. Growth is speeding up, but it is eating into gross margin.

A quarter well above plan

Cloudflare guided to $736 million to $737 million back in August. It beat that midpoint by $46 million.

A few numbers stood out:

Revenue growth reached 39%, its fastest in nearly four years, up from 36% in the second quarter and 34% in the first.

Non-GAAP operating margin climbed to 17.5% from 15.3% a year earlier.

Non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.38 from $0.27, and current RPO grew 37%.

CEO Matthew Prince sounded like a man who expects more. "Our engine is firing on all cylinders, and we've found an even higher gear for this next phase of growth," he said in the earnings release.

Here is that acceleration, quarter by quarter…

Cloudflare (NET): total revenue, quarterly, $ millions, Q3 2024–Q3 2026 (TIKR)

Quarterly revenue is up from $562 million a year ago, which puts Cloudflare past a $3 billion annual run rate.

The outlook carries the story

The guidance mattered even more than the beat. Cloudflare expects fourth-quarter revenue of $845 million to $846 million, about 38% above last year's $614.5 million.

Full-year guidance rose to $2.963 billion to $2.964 billion, from $2.864 billion to $2.870 billion in August. That implies roughly 37% growth for 2026, while adjusted EPS guidance moved up to $1.35.

Management also said on the earnings call that it expects a GAAP profit in the fourth quarter. Its investor day had set 2028 as the target.

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare is up 11% in a week after third-quarter revenue rose 39% to $782.5 million and its guidance beat estimates.

Earnings erased losses from Datadog's flat outlook and an AI selloff, so the gain comes from the quarter.

Gross margin slipped to 71.2% from 74.0%, and the stock still trades at a steep forward multiple.

Zscaler's Dec. 2 report comes next, then Cloudflare's first 2027 outlook, likely in February.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock is up 11% in the past week.

On Nov. 4, Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ) guided to flat fourth-quarter revenue, dragging cloud stocks down. The next day, the AI selloff after Democrats swept Congress hit Cloudflare again. Earnings won those losses back on Friday, and Monday added another 9%, more than three times the Nasdaq's gain. What's left is the quarter, and Zscaler (ZS:NASDAQ), its rival in zero-trust security, will want to read it closely.

Growth sped up, and Cloudflare expects more

Third-quarter revenue rose 39% to $782.5 million. CEO Matthew Prince was thrilled in the earnings release: "Our engine is firing on all cylinders, and we've found an even higher gear for this next phase of growth."

Cloudflare expects fourth-quarter revenue of $845 million to $846 million, against analysts' $798.2 million. Datadog's fourth-quarter guide of $1.19 billion to $1.20 billion, by contrast, is flat with the quarter it just reported. So far, the slowdown investors feared on Nov. 4 looks like Datadog's own.

Analysts have already raised their 2027 revenue estimate to $3.89 billion, from $3.70 billion going into the report:

Cloudflare (NET): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

That's about 31% growth on Cloudflare's new $2.96 billion outlook for 2026, down from about 37% this year. I'd expect it to keep rising.

Margins are slipping, and the stock isn't cheap

Gross margin held above 76% from 2021 through 2024, then slipped to 74.5% last year:

Cloudflare (NET): gross margin (%), fiscal 2021-2025 (TIKR)

It fell to 71.2% in the third quarter, from 74.0% a year ago. Management puts that down to its lower-margin developer products growing fastest. Higher estimates cut its forward P/E to 154x by Friday's close. Monday's jump puts it back around 170x, close to its 173x average since mid-2023.

Zscaler reports first, on Dec. 2. Leaving out its Red Canary acquisition, its annual recurring revenue grew 20% in the year to July 31, and it expects 16.6% to 17.4% growth this fiscal year. If it holds that pace, security budgets are growing for both companies. A slowdown there would suggest Cloudflare is taking share.

Cloudflare's best quarter ever hit with a growing margin challenge

I know you spend some time online, moving between sites and other websites. And I'm certain that now and then, a page has asked you to confirm you're human before letting you through. You might see it as a small interruption, but it shows how much work goes on behind the scenes to keep websites accessible while filtering out automated traffic.

You see that check? Often happens through Cloudflare, which serves 115 million web requests a second on average from data centers in more than 340 cities. And there's a reason. 

Imperva's 2026 Bad Bot Report found automated programs generated a record 53% of requests over the past year, with bad bots alone accounting for 40%. Another tally shows daily AI-enabled bot attacks rose from 2 million to 25 million in 2025 — a 12.5x year-over-year increase.

CEO Matthew Prince said the third quarter was "Cloudflare's best quarter ever," as revenue crossed a $3 billion annualized pace at $782.5 million, up 39%. It is its fastest growth in nearly four years. However, growing this fast has a price.

We have built the development platform for the AI-powered Internet—and as digital threats escalate, organizations of every size continue to rely on Cloudflare for protection.

Cloudflare posts a record quarter, and Morgan Stanley stays bullish

In a note Morgan Stanley shared with me at TheStreet, it maintained an Overweight rating and a $370 price target on Cloudflare (NET). That's a 37% increase from Nov. 6 close of $268.75, according to Yahoo Finance. The bank said broad-based execution and momentum in developer and security products support durable growth. 

In fact, revenue beat Cloudflare's own guidance midpoint by $46 million, or 6.2%, and was more than 6% above consensus, while contracted future revenue grew 37%. Fourth-quarter guidance of $845-$846 million implies 38% growth, about 6% above consensus.

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare fell 32% from its Oct. 9 record close to its Nov. 5 close, just before its third-quarter report. After the report, Goldman Sachs kept its Buy rating and $420 price target, 56% above the Nov. 6 close.

Revenue grew 39% in the third quarter, the fastest in nearly four years, and management now expects a GAAP profit in the fourth quarter.

Heading into the report, the consensus price target had risen to $345 from $240 a year ago, and analysts' 2027 earnings estimate had risen to $1.69 a share from $1.59 three months earlier.

Goldman's $420 works out to 284x forward earnings, well above any quarter-end multiple since mid-2023, so the Street's $345 average is the more realistic target for the next year.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) fell 32% from its Oct. 9 record close of $360.93 to $244.51 on Nov. 5, the day of its third-quarter report. Then it reported 39% revenue growth, its fastest in nearly four years, and shares rose 9.91% to $268.75 on Nov. 6. Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating and $420 price target, 56% above that close.

A rough few weeks for AI stocks

A software selloff hit cloud stocks in late October. Then Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress after a campaign in which candidates from both parties went after AI data centers. And on Nov. 5, hours before the report, cybersecurity stocks sold off again as the AI trade unwound.

Goldman's case rests on the guide

Goldman's Gabriela Borges stuck with her call on Nov. 6, and the numbers gave her plenty to work with. Third-quarter revenue of $782.5 million beat Wall Street's $738.5 million estimate by 6%. The fourth-quarter outlook of $845 million to $846 million sits 6% above the Street on revenue, and the 43-cent adjusted EPS guide runs 13% ahead, based on consensus figures compiled by Benzinga. CEO Matthew Prince called it "Cloudflare's best quarter ever."

Cloudflare also expects a GAAP profit in that quarter. CFO Thomas Seifert said that would come "significantly earlier" than the 2028 deadline the company set at its investor day. It is a forecast, not a result yet.

Does $420 add up?

Analysts didn't follow the stock down. Heading into the report, the consensus target had risen to $345 from $240 a year ago, 28% above the Nov. 6 close.

Cloudflare (NET): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

Before the report, the highest of those targets was $430, so Goldman's sits near the top.

Earnings estimates have gone up too. Analysts expect $1.69 a share of normalized earnings in 2027, up from $1.59 three months earlier.

Cloudflare (NET): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

The new guidance should push those estimates up again: management now expects $1.35 a share of non-GAAP earnings for 2026, above the $1.26 consensus going into the report.

Goldman needs a lot more from the multiple, though. At the Nov. 2 close, Cloudflare traded at 179x the $1.48 a share analysts expect over the next twelve months, close to its 173x average at quarter-ends since mid-2023. Goldman's $420 works out to 284x those same earnings, well above the 235x high over that stretch.

Good enough for a rebound

The cash picture is thinner than the adjusted numbers suggest. Cloudflare paid $174.1 million in stock compensation and related payroll taxes in the third quarter, more than twice its $82.1 million of free cash flow.

Goldman has the business right, and the Street's $345 average looks well within reach. But $420 within a year needs investors to pay more for Cloudflare's earnings than at any quarter-end since mid-2023. That is hard to underwrite while the company still posted a $34.1 million GAAP net loss in the third quarter.

The fourth-quarter report, likely in February, will show whether that GAAP profit arrives.

MACD divergence is a strong market signal, revealing a shifting balance that, in this case, was from bullish to bearish. The ensuing correction was sharp and severe, shaving more than 20% off the stock price within a matter of weeks, and now a new signal is emerging.

→ The Ugly Truth Behind SoundHound's Q3 Results

Cloudflare's early November price action was volatile and hit new lows but triggered a rebound rally that formed an interesting candlestick pattern. That is, an unusually large candle with a long lower wick and a smallish body, verging on a Doji, with the long lower wick (also known as a Shadow) revealing a buying situation - price action hit a low and then rebounded as activity switched from selling to buying.

The read is that the lower candle wick points to the bottom of the price correction, likely near the session's lows. Coinciding signals include a support target at $255 and a developing uptrend, which the candle pattern also reflects. The questions now are how quickly a sustainable rally can develop, and whether price action will retest the lows before it does. Questions the Q3 earnings report can help answer.

→ Lemonade's Revenue Soars 73%—So Why Did Its Stock Turn Sour After Earnings?

Cloudflare sends signal
Cloudflare's Q3 Growth Accelerates as Management Raises Guidance

Cloudflare had a solid third quarter, accelerating growth to 39.2% year over year (YOY) and outpacing consensus by more than 5.5 percentage points.

→ Anthropic's S-1 Strengthens the Case for Broadcom's AI Growth

Cloudflare's growth reflected a 110% YOY increase in new paying customer additions and stronger spending among existing customers, with dollar-based net retention rising three percentage points YOY to 122%.

Net new annual recurring revenue (ARR), a measure of visible revenue, grew an eye-popping 73.8%, while quarterly revenue surpassed $782 million, pushing Cloudflare's annualized revenue run rate above $3 billion.

NEW YORK, Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Equity Insider News Commentary - All four of the main U.S. stock benchmarks were trading higher in the first half hour of Monday's session. As of 9:57 a.m. ET, the S&P 500 was up 125.70 points, or 1.70%, at 7,502.56, the Nasdaq Composite was up 539.15 points, or 2.19%, at 25,118.58, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 727.61 points, or 1.42%, at 52,013.34, and the small cap Russell 2000 was up 53.59 points, or 1.95%, at 2,807.70. The broad start comes one day before the Bureau of Labor Statistics is scheduled to publish its October Consumer Price Index, and several large companies that reported results over the past two weeks were among the stocks moving in early trading. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN), Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL), Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET), Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), and Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. (NYSE: RCL).

Equity Insider

A week built around inflation data

The calendar is a large part of the backdrop. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics release schedule, the Consumer Price Index for October 2026 is due at 8:30 a.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, and the Producer Price Index for October 2026 follows at 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday, November 13.

Those reports land about two weeks after the Federal Reserve's most recent policy decision. In its October 28 statement, the Federal Open Market Committee said it "decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent." The Committee also wrote that "Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace" and that "Inflation remains elevated."

Among the session's early movers were companies with fresh quarterly numbers on the table, spread across online retail and cloud computing, consumer hardware, internet infrastructure, data center networking and travel.

Retail, cloud and the iPhone

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) was up 5.33% as of 9:57 a.m. ET. In its third quarter results released October 29, the company reported that net sales increased 12% to $201.9 billion, compared with $180.2 billion in the third quarter of 2025. Operating income was $28.1 billion and operating margin was 13.9%, which Amazon called its highest operating margin ever, while AWS net sales increased 39.3% to a $184 billion annualized revenue run rate.

"Our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working, with over 39% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3 ($184 billion revenue run rate) and projected revenue growth rates of over 40% both in 2027 and in 2028," said Andy Jassy, President and CEO, Amazon.
